artists.biography: Pop Will Eat Itself (also known as PWEI or The Poppies) are an English alternative rock band, originally formed in Stourbridge in 1986, with members from Birmingham, Coventry and the Black Country. Initially known as a Grebo act, their style changed to incorporate sample driven indie and industrial rock. Their highest charting single was 1993's "Get The Girl! Kill The Baddies!". After initially disbanding in 1996, and having a brief reformation in 2005, they issued their first release in over five years in 2010.

Pop Will Eat Itself.biography: Pop Will Eat Itself (also known as PWEI or The Poppies) are an English alternative rock band, originally formed in Stourbridge in 1986, with members from Birmingham, Coventry and the Black Country. Initially known as a Grebo act, their style changed to incorporate sample driven indie and industrial rock. Their highest charting single was 1993's "Get The Girl! Kill The Baddies!". After initially disbanding in 1996, and having a brief reformation in 2005, they issued their first release in over five years in 2010.

perplexity.description:
Can U Dig It?" is a single by Pop Will Eat Itself, released in 1989 as part of their second studio album, This Is the Day...This Is the Hour...This Is This!. The track exemplifies the band's innovative fusion of electronic, hip hop, and rock elements, characterized by aggressive sampling, driving beats, and irreverent lyrics. Drawing from punk rock, heavy metal, and disco influences, the song stands out for its energetic production and sharp cultural references, reflecting the eclectic style that defined the band's approach during this period.

Musically, "Can U Dig It?" helped solidify Pop Will Eat Itself's reputation for blending genres in a way that was both inventive and accessible. As one of the three major singles from the album—alongside "Def. Con. One" and "Wise Up! Sucker"—it played a key role in the band's breakthrough, contributing to the album's peak at #24 on the UK Albums Chart and #169 on the US Billboard 200. The song received critical acclaim for its humor, originality, and self-contained sonic universe, with producer Flood's influence widely noted. Released on RCA Records, "Can U Dig It?" remains a signature track in Pop Will Eat Itself's discography and a standout example of late-1980s British alternative rock.
